title: One Dead Whale Can Feed Life on the Seafloor for 50 Years

scenes.text: One dead whale can feed life on the seafloor for 50 years.
When a whale dies, its body can sink kilometres to the bottom. Scientists call it a whale fall.
First come hagfish, sleeper sharks and crabs. They strip the flesh in up to two years.
Then bone-eating worms move in. One can spend up to ten years on a skeleton.
Finally, bacteria break down fats in the bones, and that feeds clams and tube worms for decades.

scenes.text: One whale. Fifty years of dinner.

description:
When a whale dies and sinks to the seabed, its carcass becomes a whale fall that can sustain deep-sea life for decades.
Scavengers strip the flesh in up to two years, bone-eating Osedax worms work on the skeleton, and bacteria-based communities can last up to 50 years.
Which deep-sea creature would you most want to see?
